You plan days of errands in San Francisco for people without a car. They travel by Muni (buses, Muni Metro, cable cars), BART, and on foot.

Choose one specific store for each errand and the order to visit them so the person finishes everything as early as possible. Respect store opening hours, the time each errand takes, any deadlines, and when they must reach their final destination. If the errands cannot all be done under those constraints, say so.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"feasible": true, "stops": [{"category": "<errand category>", "store_name": "<name>", "address": "<street address>", "poi_id": "<the store's id if ids were given, else null>"}], "reason": null}

- One stop per errand, in visiting order. Use exactly these category names: "bike_shop" (bike shop), "post_office" (post office), "supermarket" (supermarket), "dry_cleaning" (dry cleaner), "pharmacy" (pharmacy), "bookstore" (bookstore).
- Give each store's name and its street address in San Francisco.
- If it is impossible, reply {"feasible": false, "stops": [], "reason": "<why>"}.

It's Friday, October 9, and I'm heading out from Haight & Fillmore (Haight) around 8:15 pm. No car today: just Muni, BART and walking. Today I need to pick up my dry cleaning (about 5 minutes), grab my prescription from a pharmacy (about 10 minutes), mail a package at a post office (about 15 minutes), pick up groceries at a supermarket (about 20 minutes), pick up a book I ordered at a bookstore (about 15 minutes), and buy a new inner tube at a bike shop (about 20 minutes). When I'm done I'm meeting a friend at 3rd & 22nd (Dogpatch). Which specific stores should I go to, and in what order, so I'm done as early as possible? If it can't all be done, tell me it's impossible and why.
